label: def:fundamental-object
title: Fundamental object
html:
Definition. Fundamental object

Let \mathbf{C} be an R-linear rigid monoidal category. A fundamental object is an object V \in \mathbf{C} equipped with a volume form

  \epsilon \colon V \otimes V \longrightarrow \mathbf{1}

— the categorical determinant \Lambda^2 V \to \mathbf{1} — together with an adjoint coform \eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to V \otimes V satisfying the two snake identities. Thus \epsilon exhibits V as its own dual: a symplectic self-dual object, the datum that distinguishes \mathrm{SL}_2 / \mathrm{SU}(2) from \mathrm{GL}_2 [deligne1990].

Under a fibre functor the volume constraint forces \mathrm{rank}(V) = 2, so V is simple of categorical dimension 2: in \mathrm{SU}(2) it is V = V_{1/2} \cong \mathbb{C}^2, every other simple object is an exterior or symmetric power of V, and V tensor-generates \mathbf{C} (see the role of V).
